name: Opal asset category slices + model-level Opal detection (primary vs custom)
description: Re-cut the three MDPF served views (aum-metrics.json / account-distribution.json / aggregate-aua-timeseries.json) into Opal asset CATEGORIES, with drilldowns -- the first and most wanted being PRIMARY vs CUSTOM MODELS, so the non-archetypal Opal models that appear in the mix (the Anna account is the named specimen) become manageable rather than anomalous. Depends on detecting 'Opal' at MODEL/constituent level rather than only at top-level STRATEGY level.

open_at_andrew: ⚠ CATEGORY LIST DISCREPANCY -- HIS WORD vs A SPEC HE MAY NOT HAVE RATIFIED, surfaced not adjudicated. Andrew 2026-08-07 named FIVE categories: 'Alternative, Client, SMA, Models, Insurance'. 4.0.0_SA_CRO's MDPF_PORTFOLIO_ONTOLOGY_AND_SLEEVE_ATTRIBUTION_SPEC_20260805.md:35-36 and :88-92 instead specifies 'Models, Strategy, Alternative, Client, Insurance' and EXPLICITLY EXCLUDES SMA, verbatim :46-48: 'SMA is not a category in this framework. Every account in the classified population is inherently an SMA, so SMA describes the common account structure and provides no discriminatory value.' A Strategy account is classified `strategy`, not `sma`. >> SO THE SPEC SUBSTITUTES `Strategy` FOR HIS `SMA`, on a non-discrimination argument. That is a defensible taxonomy position (Rule 24: a value every member carries partitions nothing) AND it overrides a category the principal named. HIS CALL, not the spec's and not mine. measured_scope_facts: THE MECHANISM ALREADY EXISTS AS A DESIGN -- 0.7.0_AE_CloudOps~Z, BRIEF_COTTONWOOD_OPAL_CONSTITUENT_ATTRIBUTION_20260807.md @924c3b669 (00:47Z). THE ROOT CAUSE IT NAMES IS THE SAME AXIS: `opal_ids = set(roster[roster.is_opal].model_id)` where 'roster = TOP-LEVEL strategies only' (:21). Its recommendation (:131-132) is to apply `is_opal` AT THE LEAF and keep non-Opal leaves visible with `is_opal=False` -- which is exactly what 0.4.0_DS implemented today as a DISJUNCTION. So the strategy-level -> model-level move is already half-done in production as of 2026-08-07.

THE UNBUILT HALF IS §7, 'THE DELTA SYSTEM -- recursive by construction, and NOT a monitor'. Four parts: (a) EXTEND THE CONSTITUENT WALK TO BE FULLY RECURSIVE (:153 -- the current scan depth is limited, so nested custom models are invisible); (b) PERSIST the constituent set with its hash in the run manifest, every `(child_model_id, child_model_name, is_opal, depth, parent_ids[])` (:156-157); (c) the DELTA is a set-difference against the prior run's manifest, computed BY THE PRODUCER and recorded as manifest rows `constituents_added`/`constituents_removed` (:158-160); (d) FAIL-CLOSED when a constituent is `is_opal=True` AND absent from the crosswalk (:161).

⭐ THAT §7 DESIGN IS WHAT ANSWERS ANDREW'S FIRST-PRIORITY DRILLDOWN. `depth` + `parent_ids[]` per constituent IS the primary-vs-custom discriminator -- a model appearing only as a nested constituent under another strategy is structurally distinguishable from one that is itself a top-level roster entry. The Anna-account class of non-archetypal Opal models is exactly what a recursive walk surfaces and a top-level roster scan cannot.

⚠ NAME-TOKEN CAVEAT, LOAD-BEARING AND FLAGGED BY THE BRIEF'S OWN AUTHOR (:166-168): `is_opal_name` is a SUBSTRING test, so it 'will match any future model containing "opal" anywhere'. Any category system built on it inherits that fragility -- a vendor naming an unrelated product with the token silently joins the Opal population. The detector must REPORT what it matched on, not merely that it matched.

THE DESIGN RESPECTS THE ALARM MORATORIUM BY CONSTRUCTION and says so: §7 is 'an assertion that lands as DATA in the run manifest' that fail-closes the build -- NOT a monitor, alarm or checker. That framing is correct and must survive into any TO; the moratorium (Andrew-direct 2026-07-28) is standing.

THE OTHER AXES ANDREW REMEMBERED ARE REAL AND ARE NOT WHERE HE THOUGHT. He guessed repo-root projects/MDPF*; measured, `advisory_scope` occurs in exactly 2 files, both CRO's: org/tier1_exec/4.0.0_SA_CRO/RECON_REGISTER.md and the ontology spec above, which at :44 defines 'independent `selection_origin`, `advisory_scope`, and `fee_basis` classifications'. The repo-root projects/ dir holds only ADVI_REFACTOR, ATOM_DECOMP and MDPF_PROPVALIDATION -- no MDPF ontology folder.

THE SPEC ALSO SUPERSEDES AN EARLIER FOUR-SEGMENT TAXONOMY: docs/architecture/MDPF_GLOBAL_PRD.md's 'ETF Models, SMA Strategies, Custom Models, and the Non-Model...' (:24, :53). So 'Custom Models' already exists as a named segment in the older PRD -- the new work is not inventing the concept, it is re-grounding it on a per-constituent structural fact instead of a segment label.
